title.zh: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十二 盛庸 平安 何福 顧成
title.en: Volume 144 Biographies 32: Cheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng
title.raw: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十二 盛庸 平安 何福 顧成 Volume 144 Biographies 32: Cheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng

sentences.zh: 盛庸平安何福顧成

translations.literal: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, and Gu Cheng

sentences.zh: 盛庸，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong — it is not known from where he came.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，累官至都指揮。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, he rose through successive posts to regional commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongwu Emperor he rose through the ranks until he reached the post of regional commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 建文初，以參將從耿炳文伐燕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, as a deputy general he followed Geng Bingwen in the campaign against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign he served as a deputy general under Geng Bingwen in the campaign against the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 李景隆代炳文，遂隸景隆麾下。

translations.literal: Li Jinglong replaced Bingwen, and he thereupon came under Jinglong's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jinglong replaced Geng Bingwen, Sheng Yong was placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，景隆敗於白溝河，走濟南。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Jinglong was defeated at the White Ditch River and fled to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Jianwen, Li Jinglong was defeated at the White Ditch River and retreated to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 燕師隨至，景隆復南走。

translations.literal: The Yan army followed in pursuit, and Jinglong again fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces pursued, and Li Jinglong fled south once more.

sentences.zh: 庸與參政鐵鉉悉力固守，燕師攻圍三月不克。

translations.literal: Yong and the participating secretary Tie Xuan exerted their full strength in defense; the Yan army besieged them for three months without taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong and the participating secretary Tie Xuan threw all their strength into the defense, and the Yan army besieged Jinan for three months without success.

sentences.zh: 庸、鉉乘夜出兵掩擊，燕眾大敗，解圍去。

translations.literal: Yong and Xuan took advantage of night to lead troops out in a surprise attack; the Yan forces suffered a great defeat and lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong and Tie Xuan led a night sortie that caught the Yan army by surprise; the besiegers were routed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乘勝復德州。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, they recovered Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Following up on their victory, they recaptured Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，論功封歷城侯，祿千石。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, his merits were assessed and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Licheng with an income of one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was rewarded for his service with enfeoffment as Marquis of Licheng and a stipend of one thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 尋命為平燕將軍，充總兵官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed General for the Pacification of Yan and made supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General for the Pacification of Yan and given overall command of the army.

sentences.zh: 陳暉、平安為左右副總兵，馬溥、徐真為左右參將，進鉉兵部尚書參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Chen Hui and Ping An served as left and right deputy commanders-in-chief; Ma Pu and Xu Zhen as left and right deputy generals; Xuan was promoted to Minister of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui and Ping An were made his left and right deputy commanders, Ma Pu and Xu Zhen his left and right deputy generals, and Tie Xuan was promoted to Minister of War to advise on strategy.

sentences.zh: 時吳傑、平安守定州，庸駐德州，徐凱屯滄州，為犄角。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Jie and Ping An held Dingzhou, Yong was stationed at Dezhou, and Xu Kai encamped at Cangzhou, forming a pincer arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie and Ping An held Dingzhou, Sheng Yong was based at Dezhou, and Xu Kai at Cangzhou, their positions forming a mutually supporting triangle.

sentences.zh: 是冬，燕兵襲滄州，破，擒凱。

translations.literal: That winter the Yan army raided Cangzhou, broke through, and captured Kai.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yan army struck Cangzhou, overran the garrison, and captured Xu Kai.

sentences.zh: 掠其輜重，進薄濟寧。

translations.literal: They plundered the baggage train and advanced to press upon Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the supply train and pressed on toward Jinan.

sentences.zh: 庸引兵屯東昌以邀之，背城而陣。

translations.literal: Yong led his troops to encamp at Dongchang to intercept them and drew up his battle line with the city at his back.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong marched to Dongchang to block their advance and drew up his army with its back to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 燕王帥兵直前薄庸軍左翼，不動。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan led his troops straight forward to press upon the left wing of Yong's army, which did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan led his troops straight at the left wing of Sheng Yong's line, which held firm without yielding.

sentences.zh: 復沖中堅，庸開陣縱王入，圍之數重。

translations.literal: He then charged the center; Yong opened his formation and let the Prince enter, then surrounded him in layer upon layer.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove at the center of the line; Sheng Yong opened his ranks to let the Prince in and closed them around him in rings of encirclement.

sentences.zh: 燕將朱能帥番騎來救，王乘間突圍出。

translations.literal: The Yan general Zhu Neng led barbarian cavalry to the rescue, and the Prince seized an opening and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general Zhu Neng led his Mongol cavalry to the rescue, and the Prince found a gap and fought his way out.

sentences.zh: 而燕軍為火器所傷甚眾，大將張玉死於陣。

translations.literal: But very many of the Yan army were wounded by firearms, and the great general Zhang Yu died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army suffered heavy casualties from gunfire, and their great general Zhang Yu was killed in the battle.

sentences.zh: 王獨以百騎殿，退至館陶。

translations.literal: The Prince alone, with a hundred horsemen as rearguard, withdrew to Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince retreated to Guantao with only a hundred horsemen covering his rear.

sentences.zh: 庸檄吳傑、平安自真定遮燕歸路。

translations.literal: Yong sent orders to Wu Jie and Ping An to move from Zhending to block the Yan army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong dispatched orders for Wu Jie and Ping An to march from Zhending and cut off the Yan army's retreat.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，傑、平安戰深州不利，燕師始得歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Jie and Ping An fought at Shenzhou with an unfavorable outcome, and only then did the Yan army manage to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Wu Jie and Ping An fought at Shenzhou without success, and only then was the Yan army able to make its way home.

sentences.zh: 是役也，燕精銳喪失幾盡，庸軍聲大振，帝為享廟告捷。

translations.literal: In this battle the elite troops of Yan were nearly all lost; the reputation of Yong's army rose greatly, and the Emperor offered sacrifices at the ancestral temple to announce the victory.
translations.idiomatic: In this engagement the Yan army's elite forces were nearly wiped out; Sheng Yong's troops won great renown, and the Emperor celebrated the victory with offerings at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 三月，燕兵復南出保定。

translations.literal: In the third month the Yan army again marched south out of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Yan army marched south again from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 庸營夾河。

translations.literal: Yong encamped on the Jia River.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong encamped along the Jia River.

sentences.zh: 王將輕騎來覘，掠陣而過。

translations.literal: The Prince led light cavalry to reconnoiter and swept past the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince rode out with a light cavalry detachment to scout the enemy lines and galloped along the front of the formation.

sentences.zh: 庸遣千騎追之，為燕兵射卻。

translations.literal: Yong sent a thousand horsemen in pursuit, but they were driven back by Yan archers.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong sent a thousand horsemen in pursuit, but Yan archers drove them back.

sentences.zh: 及戰，庸軍列盾以進。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Yong's army advanced in shield formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle began, Sheng Yong's troops advanced behind a wall of shields.

sentences.zh: 王令步卒先攻，騎兵乘間馳入。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered the infantry to attack first, and the cavalry seized an opening and charged in.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent his infantry forward first, then sent his cavalry charging through the gaps they opened.

sentences.zh: 庸麾軍力戰，斬其將譚淵。

translations.literal: Yong directed his army in fierce combat and beheaded the enemy general Tan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong led his troops in fierce fighting and killed the Yan general Tan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 而朱能、張武等帥眾殊死鬥。

translations.literal: But Zhu Neng, Zhang Wu, and others led their troops in a fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng, Zhang Wu, and others rallied their men and fought with desperate fury.

sentences.zh: 王以勁騎貫陣與能合。

translations.literal: The Prince, with crack cavalry, pierced through the formation and joined with Neng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince broke through the enemy line with his finest cavalry and linked up with Zhu Neng.

sentences.zh: 庸部驍將莊得、皂旗張等俱戰死。

translations.literal: Among Yong's forces the valiant generals Zhuang De, Zhang of the Black Banner, and others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong's crack generals Zhuang De, Zhang of the Black Banner Company, and others were all killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 是日，燕軍幾敗。

translations.literal: That day the Yan army nearly suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Yan army came close to total defeat.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，燕軍東北，庸軍西南，自辰至未，互勝負。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; the Yan army was to the northeast and Yong's army to the southwest; from the hour of chen to the hour of wei, victory alternated between them.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day, the Yan army to the northeast and Sheng Yong's to the southwest; from mid-morning until mid-afternoon the advantage shifted back and forth.

sentences.zh: 兩軍皆疲，將士各坐息。

translations.literal: Both armies were exhausted, and officers and men alike sat down to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies were exhausted, and officers and men on both sides sat down where they stood to catch their breath.

sentences.zh: 復起戰，忽東北風大起，飛塵蔽天。

translations.literal: They rose to fight again, when suddenly a great northeast wind arose and flying dust blotted out the sky.
translations.idiomatic: They took up the fight again, but suddenly a fierce northeast wind sprang up and whirling dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 燕兵乘風大呼，左右橫擊。

translations.literal: The Yan troops, riding the wind, shouted loudly and struck from left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops rode the wind, shouting as they charged, and struck from both flanks.

sentences.zh: 庸大敗走還德州，自是氣沮。

translations.literal: Yong suffered a great defeat and fled back to Dezhou; from this time his spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong was routed and fled back to Dezhou, and from that day his army's fighting spirit never recovered.

sentences.zh: 已而燕將李遠焚糧艘於沛縣，庸軍遂乏餉。

translations.literal: Before long the Yan general Li Yuan burned the grain transports at Peixian, and Yong's army then lacked provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yan general Li Yuan burned the grain barges at Peixian, and Sheng Yong's army was left without supplies.

sentences.zh: 明年，靈璧戰敗，平安等被執。

translations.literal: The following year, defeated at Lingbi, Ping An and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the defeat at Lingbi, Ping An and others were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 庸獨引軍而南，列戰艦淮南岸。

translations.literal: Yong alone led his army south and arrayed warships along the south bank of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong alone led his army south and lined his warships along the southern bank of the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 燕將邱福等潛濟，出庸後。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Qiu Fu and others crossed secretly and emerged behind Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Qiu Fu and others forded the river in secret and appeared in Sheng Yong's rear.

sentences.zh: 庸不能支，退為守江計。

translations.literal: Yong could not hold his ground and withdrew to plan for the defense of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold his position, Sheng Yong fell back to organize the defense of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 燕兵渡淮，由盱眙陷揚州。

translations.literal: The Yan army crossed the Huai, and via Xuyi captured Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army crossed the Huai, took Xuyi, and captured Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庸禦戰於六合及浦子口，皆失利，都督陳瑄帥舟師降燕，燕兵遂渡江。

translations.literal: Yong met them in battle at Liuhe and Puzikou, but in each case was defeated; the regional commander Chen Xuan led the fleet in surrender to Yan, and the Yan army then crossed the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong fought them at Liuhe and Puzikou but was beaten both times; the regional commander Chen Xuan surrendered his fleet to the Yan, and the Yan army crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 庸倉卒聚海艘出高資港迎戰，復敗，軍益潰散。

translations.literal: Yong in haste gathered seagoing vessels and sailed out from Gaozigang to give battle, but was again defeated and his army dispersed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong hastily assembled a fleet and sailed from Gaozigang to give battle, but was defeated again and his army broke apart completely.

sentences.zh: 平安，滁人，小字保兒。

translations.literal: Ping An was a man of Chuzhou; his childhood name was Bao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An was a native of Chuzhou; his childhood name was Bao'er.

sentences.zh: 父定，從太祖起兵，官濟寧衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His father Ding followed the Taizu in raising the army and held the post of assistant commander of the Jining guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding had followed the founding emperor in the uprising and served as assistant commander of the Jining guard.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春下元都，戰沒。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in the descent upon the Yuan capital and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun in the campaign against the Yuan capital and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 安初為太祖養子，驍勇善戰，力舉數百斤。

translations.literal: An was at first the Taizu's adopted son; he was valiant and skilled in battle, and could lift several hundred jin in strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An had originally been adopted by the founding emperor; he was fierce in battle and reputed to lift weights of several hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，遷密雲指揮使，進右軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post, was transferred to commander of Miyun, and advanced to assistant regional commander of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post, was transferred to commander of Miyun, and was promoted to assistant regional commander of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 燕兵圍濟南。

translations.literal: The Yan army besieged Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army besieged Jinan.

sentences.zh: 安營單家橋，謀出御河奪燕餉舟。

translations.literal: An encamped at Danjia Bridge and planned to go out via the Imperial Canal to seize the Yan supply boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An encamped at Danjia Bridge and planned a sortie along the Imperial Canal to seize the Yan supply fleet.

sentences.zh: 又選善水卒五千人渡河，將攻德州。

translations.literal: He also selected five thousand skilled water soldiers to cross the river, intending to attack Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected five thousand skilled river fighters to cross the river with the intention of striking at Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 圍乃解。

translations.literal: The siege was thereupon lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 安與吳傑進屯定州。

translations.literal: An and Wu Jie advanced to encamp at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An and Wu Jie advanced and encamped at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，燕敗盛庸於夾河，回軍與安戰單家橋。

translations.literal: The following year, having defeated Sheng Yong at the Jia River, the Yan army returned and fought An at Danjia Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after defeating Sheng Yong at the Jia River, the Yan army turned back and fought Ping An at Danjia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 安奮擊大破之，擒其將薛祿。

translations.literal: An fought with fierce energy and inflicted a great defeat, capturing the enemy general Xue Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An attacked with furious energy and routed them, capturing the Yan general Xue Lu.

sentences.zh: 無何，逸去。

translations.literal: Before long, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, however, Xue Lu escaped.

sentences.zh: 再戰滹沱河，又破之。

translations.literal: They fought again at the Hutuo River and he again inflicted defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at the Hutuo River, and Ping An defeated them once more.

sentences.zh: 安於陣中縛木為樓，高數丈，戰酣，輒登樓望，發強弩射燕軍，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: An bound timbers into a tower within the battle formation, several zhang in height; when the fighting grew fierce he would ascend the tower to survey the field and loose powerful crossbows at the Yan army, and very many were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An had a wooden tower several zhang high erected within his battle line; when the fighting grew fierce he would climb it to survey the field and loose powerful crossbows at the Yan ranks, killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 忽大風起，發屋拔樹，聲如雷。

translations.literal: Suddenly a great wind arose, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a violent wind sprang up, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees with a roar like thunder.

sentences.zh: 都指揮鄧戩、陳鵬等陷敵中，安遂敗走真定。

translations.literal: The regional commanders Deng Zhan, Chen Peng, and others were trapped within the enemy ranks, and An thereupon was defeated and fled to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commanders Deng Zhan and Chen Peng were cut off behind enemy lines, and Ping An was driven back to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 燕王與南軍數大戰，每親身陷陣，所向皆靡，惟安與庸二軍屢挫之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan fought many great battles with the southern army; each time he personally entered the thick of the fight and wherever he went all were swept away — only the armies of An and Yong repeatedly checked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan fought many pitched battles against the southern forces, always plunging in person into the thick of the fighting and sweeping all before him — only the armies of Ping An and Sheng Yong repeatedly turned him back.

sentences.zh: 滹沱之戰，矢集王旗如蝟毛。

translations.literal: At the battle of the Hutuo, arrows clustered on the Prince's banner like hedgehog quills.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle on the Hutuo, arrows clustered on the Prince's standard thick as the quills on a hedgehog.

sentences.zh: 王使人送旗北平，諭世子謹藏，以示後世。

translations.literal: The Prince sent a man to deliver the banner to Beiping, instructing the heir apparent to keep it carefully as a token for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent the banner to Beiping with orders that the heir apparent preserve it carefully as a memorial for future generations.

sentences.zh: 顧成已先被執在燕，見而泣曰：「臣自少從軍，今老矣，多歷戰陣，未嘗見若此也。」

translations.literal: Gu Cheng had already been captured earlier and was in the Yan camp; seeing it he wept and said, "Your servant has followed the army since youth; now I am old and have passed through many battlefields, yet never have I seen the like of this."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng, who had already been taken prisoner and was in the Yan camp, wept when he saw it and said, "I have followed the colors since I was young, and I am an old man now who has seen many battlefields — yet I have never seen anything like this."

sentences.zh: 逾月，燕師出大名。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the Yan army marched out from Daming.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later the Yan army marched out from Daming.

sentences.zh: 安與庸及吳傑等分兵擾其餉道。

translations.literal: An, Yong, Wu Jie, and others divided their forces to harass the Yan supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An, Sheng Yong, Wu Jie, and others divided their forces to raid the Yan supply lines.

sentences.zh: 燕王患之，遣指揮武勝上書於朝，請撤安等息兵，為緩師計。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was troubled by this and sent the commander Wu Sheng to submit a memorial to the court, requesting the withdrawal of An and the others to cease hostilities, as a stratagem to slow the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, alarmed by these raids, sent the commander Wu Sheng to the court with a memorial asking that Ping An and the others be recalled to halt the fighting — a ruse to gain time.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 燕王亦決計南下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan also resolved to march south.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan meanwhile resolved to push south regardless.

sentences.zh: 遣李遠等潛走沛縣，焚糧舟，掠彰德，破尾尖寨，諭降林縣。

translations.literal: He dispatched Li Yuan and others to slip secretly to Peixian, burn the grain boats, plunder Zhangde, break Tailijian stockade, and persuade Linxian to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Yuan and others secretly to Peixian to burn the grain barges, then raided Zhangde, stormed Tailijian stockade, and accepted the surrender of Linxian.

sentences.zh: 時安在真定，度北平空虛，帥萬騎直走北平。

translations.literal: At that time An was at Zhending; judging Beiping to be empty, he led ten thousand horsemen straight for Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An was then at Zhending; judging that Beiping lay undefended, he led ten thousand cavalry straight for the Yan capital.

sentences.zh: 至平村，去城五十里而軍。

translations.literal: He reached Pingcun and encamped fifty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Pingcun and encamped fifty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 燕王懼，遣劉江等馳還救。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was alarmed and dispatched Liu Jiang and others to gallop back to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was alarmed and sent Liu Jiang and others racing back to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 安戰不利，引還。

translations.literal: An fought without success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An met them in battle without success and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時大同守將房昭引兵入紫荊關，據易州西水寨以窺北平，安自真定餉之。

translations.literal: At that time the Datong garrison commander Fang Zhao led troops through Zijing Pass, seized the Xishui stockade at Yizhou to spy on Beiping, and An supplied him from Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Datong garrison commander Fang Zhao marched through Zijing Pass and seized the Xishui stockade west of Yizhou to threaten Beiping, and Ping An supplied his forces from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 八月，燕兵北歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Yan army returned north.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Yan army marched north again.

sentences.zh: 安及燕將李彬戰於楊村，敗之。

translations.literal: An fought the Yan general Li Bin at Yangcun and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An fought the Yan general Li Bin at Yangcun and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 四年，燕兵復南下，破蕭縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yan army again marched south and took Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwen the Yan army marched south again and captured Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 安引軍躡其後，至淝河。

translations.literal: An led his army in pursuit behind them as far as the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An pursued with his army as far as the Fei River.

sentences.zh: 燕將白義、王真、劉江迎敵。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Bai Yi, Wang Zhen, and Liu Jiang came out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Bai Yi, Wang Zhen, and Liu Jiang came out to give battle.

sentences.zh: 安轉戰，斬真。

translations.literal: An fought in successive engagements and beheaded Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An fought through several engagements and killed Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 真，驍將。

translations.literal: Zhen was a valiant general.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen had been one of the Prince's finest fighters.

sentences.zh: 燕王嘗曰：「諸將奮勇如王真，何事不成！

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan had once said, "If all my generals fought with the fierce courage of Wang Zhen, what undertaking could fail!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan had once said, "If all my generals fought with the fierce courage of Wang Zhen, what could we not accomplish!

sentences.zh: 」至是為安所殺。

translations.literal: " — and now he was killed by An.
translations.idiomatic: " — and now Ping An had killed him.

sentences.zh: 燕王乃身自迎戰，安部將火耳灰挺槊大呼，直前刺王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan thereupon personally came out to give battle; An's deputy general Huo'erhui brandished his spear and shouted loudly, charging straight forward to thrust at the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan then rode out to fight in person; Ping An's deputy Huo'erhui brandished his spear, shouted, and charged straight at the Prince.

sentences.zh: 馬忽蹶，被擒。

translations.literal: His horse suddenly stumbled, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: His horse stumbled suddenly and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 安稍引卻。

translations.literal: An drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An drew his forces back slightly.

sentences.zh: 已，復進至小河，張左右翼擊燕軍，斬其將陳文。

translations.literal: Before long he again advanced to the Xiao River, deployed his left and right wings to strike the Yan army, and beheaded the enemy general Chen Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he advanced again to the Xiao River, deployed both wings against the Yan army, and killed the Yan general Chen Wen.

sentences.zh: 已，復移軍齊眉山，與諸將列陣大戰。

translations.literal: Before long he again shifted his army to Qimei Mountain and, with the various generals, drew up battle lines for a great engagement.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army to Qimei Mountain and, with his fellow commanders, drew up for a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 自午至酉，又敗之。

translations.literal: From the hour of wu to the hour of you he again inflicted defeat.
translations.idiomatic: From noon until evening he routed them again.

sentences.zh: 燕諸將謀北還，圖後舉。

translations.literal: The Yan generals plotted to return north and plan a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals urged a retreat to the north and a fresh campaign later.

sentences.zh: 王不聽。

translations.literal: The Prince would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 尋阻何福軍亦至，與安合。

translations.literal: Before long He Fu's army, which had been blocking the way, also arrived and joined with An.
translations.idiomatic: Soon He Fu's army, which had been blocking the Yan advance, arrived as well and joined forces with Ping An.

sentences.zh: 燕軍益大懼，王晝夜擐甲者數日。

translations.literal: The Yan army grew all the more fearful, and for several days the Prince wore his armor day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was more alarmed than ever, and for several days the Prince slept in his armor day and night.

sentences.zh: 福欲持久老燕師，移營靈璧，深塹高壘自固。

translations.literal: Fu wished to wear down the Yan army through a prolonged standoff; he shifted camp to Lingbi, dug deep moats and raised high ramparts, and fortified himself.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu planned to wear down the Yan army in a war of attrition, moved his camp to Lingbi, and dug deep trenches behind high ramparts to hold his position.

sentences.zh: 而糧運為燕兵所陰，不得達。

translations.literal: But the grain convoys were secretly intercepted by the Yan army and could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Yan forces secretly cut his supply lines, however, and no grain reached the camp.

sentences.zh: 安分兵往迎，燕王以精騎遮安軍，分為二。

translations.literal: An divided his forces to go meet the convoys; the Prince of Yan used crack cavalry to block An's army and split it in two.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An sent troops to escort the supplies, but the Prince of Yan intercepted them with elite cavalry and cut Ping An's force in two.

sentences.zh: 福開壁來援，為高煦所敗。

translations.literal: Fu opened the stockade to come to the rescue and was defeated by Gao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu led his men out of the camp to relieve them and was defeated by Gao Xu.

sentences.zh: 諸將謀移軍淮河就糧，夜令軍中聞三炮即走。

translations.literal: The generals plotted to shift the army to the Huai River to obtain grain and ordered that at night, upon hearing three cannon shots, the troops were to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The generals decided to move toward the Huai River for supplies and gave orders that three cannon shots at night would signal a retreat.

sentences.zh: 翌日，燕軍猝薄壘，發三炮。

translations.literal: The next day the Yan army suddenly pressed upon the ramparts and fired three cannon shots.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Yan army suddenly assaulted the ramparts and fired three cannon shots.

sentences.zh: 軍中誤以為己號，爭趨門，遂大亂。

translations.literal: The army mistakenly took this for their own signal and rushed in a scramble for the gates, whereupon great disorder ensued.
translations.idiomatic: The southern troops mistook this for their own signal and stampeded for the gates, throwing the camp into chaos.

sentences.zh: 燕兵乘之，人馬墜壕塹俱滿。

translations.literal: The Yan troops seized the opportunity; men and horses fell into the moats and ditches until they were filled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army pressed the attack, and men and horses tumbled into the moats until the ditches were choked with bodies.

sentences.zh: 福單騎走，安及陳暉、馬溥、徐真、孫成等三十七人皆被執。

translations.literal: Fu fled alone on horseback; An together with Chen Hui, Ma Pu, Xu Zhen, Sun Cheng, and thirty-seven others were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu escaped alone on horseback; Ping An, Chen Hui, Ma Pu, Xu Zhen, Sun Cheng, and thirty-seven others were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文臣宦官在軍被執者又百五十余人，時四月辛巳也。

translations.literal: Civil officials and eunuchs with the army who were captured numbered more than another hundred and fifty; the time was the xinsi day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred and fifty civil officials and eunuchs with the army were also captured; the date was the xinsi day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 安久駐真定，屢敗燕兵，斬驍將數人，燕將莫敢嬰其鋒。

translations.literal: An had long been stationed at Zhending, repeatedly defeating the Yan army and beheading several valiant generals; no Yan general dared meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An had long been based at Zhending, repeatedly defeating Yan forces and killing several of their best fighters; no Yan commander dared face him head-on.

sentences.zh: 至是被擒，軍中歡呼動地，曰：「吾屬自此獲安矣！

translations.literal: When he was now captured, cheers in the army shook the earth, saying, "We from this time forward have obtained peace!
translations.idiomatic: When he was captured at last, the Yan army erupted in cheers that shook the ground: "We are safe at last!

sentences.zh: 」爭請殺安。

translations.literal: " They vied in asking to kill An.
translations.idiomatic: " Men clamored to have Ping An put to death.

sentences.zh: 燕王惜其材勇，選銳卒衛送北平，命世子及郭資等善視之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan valued his talent and courage, selected crack troops to guard and escort him to Beiping, and ordered the heir apparent and Guo Zi and others to treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan valued his ability and courage, sent picked troops to escort him to Beiping, and ordered the heir apparent and Guo Zi and others to treat him with care.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，以安為北平都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Prince ascended the throne, he appointed An regional commander of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince took the throne, he appointed Ping An regional commander of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 尋進行後府都督僉事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to assistant regional commander of the Rear Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to assistant regional commander of the Rear Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年三月，帝巡北京。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle, the Emperor toured Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle, the Emperor made a tour of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 將至，覽章奏見安名，謂左右曰：「平保兒尚在耶？

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, he perused memorials and saw An's name; he said to those at his side, "Is Ping Bao'er still alive?
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to arrive, he reviewed memorials and saw Ping An's name; he said to his attendants, "So Ping Bao'er is still alive?

sentences.zh: 」安聞之，遂自殺。

translations.literal: " When An heard of this, he thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ping An heard of this, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 命以指揮使祿給其子。

translations.literal: He ordered that the stipend of a regional commander be given to his son.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered that his son receive a commander's stipend.

sentences.zh: 何福，鳳陽人。

translations.literal: He Fu was a man of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu was a native of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，累功為金吾後衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign, through accumulated merit he became vice commander of the Jinyu Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign he rose through accumulated merit to vice commander of the Jinyu Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德征雲南，擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde in the campaign against Yunnan and was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Youde in the Yunnan campaign and was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 又從藍玉出塞，至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: He again followed Lan Yu beyond the frontier as far as Buyur Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Lan Yu on a campaign beyond the frontier as far as Buyur Lake.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，江陰侯吳高帥迤北降人南征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao led the surrendered peoples of the northern frontier in a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Hongwu, the Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao led surrendered northern tribesmen on a southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 抵沅江，眾叛，由思州出荊、樊，道渭河，欲遁歸沙漠。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yuan River, the masses rebelled; they went out through Sizhou toward Jing and Fan, took the route of the Wei River, and wished to flee back to the desert.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan River the tribesmen rebelled; they marched out through Sizhou toward Jing and Fan, followed the Wei River route, and tried to flee back to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，福與都督聶緯追擊，及諸鹿阝、延，盡殲之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Fu together with the regional commander Nie Wei pursued in attack, overtook them at Zhulu and Yan, and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year He Fu and the regional commander Nie Wei pursued them, overtook them at Zhulu and Yan, and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 移兵討平都勻蠻，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: He shifted his troops to suppress and pacify the Duyun tribes, capturing and beheading them by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army to pacify the Duyun tribes, capturing and killing them by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜平羌將軍，討越州叛蠻阿資，破降之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Qiang and campaigned against the rebellious Yuezhou tribesman Azi, defeating and accepting his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Qiang and campaigned against the rebellious Yuezhou chieftain Azi, defeating him and accepting his surrender.

sentences.zh: 擇地立柵處其眾，置寧越堡。

translations.literal: He selected a site, established stockades to settle their masses, and set up Ningyue Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a site, settled the tribes in stockades, and established Ningyue Fort.

sentences.zh: 遂平九名、九姓諸蠻。

translations.literal: He thereupon pacified the various tribes of the Nine Clans and Nine Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the tribes of the Nine Clans and Nine Surnames.

sentences.zh: 尋與都督茅鼎會兵，徇五開。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he joined forces with the regional commander Mao Ding and marched on Wukai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the regional commander Mao Ding and marched on Wukai.

sentences.zh: 未行，而畢節諸蠻復叛，大掠屯堡，殺吏士。

translations.literal: Before they set out, the tribes of Bije and others rebelled again, plundering stockade-forts on a great scale and killing officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could march, the Bije tribes rebelled again, raiding garrison posts and killing officials and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 福令畢節諸衛嚴備，而檄都督陶文等從鼎搗其巢。

translations.literal: Fu ordered the guards of Bije and others to make strict preparations, while dispatching orders to the regional commander Tao Wen and others to follow Ding in striking their nest.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu ordered the Bije garrisons to stand on alert and sent orders for the regional commander Tao Wen and others to join Mao Ding in attacking their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 擒叛酋，戮之。

translations.literal: They captured the rebellious chieftains and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the rebel chiefs and executed them.

sentences.zh: 分兵盡捕諸蠻，建堡設戍，乃趨五開。

translations.literal: They divided their forces to capture all the tribes, built forts and set garrisons, and then pressed on to Wukai.
translations.idiomatic: They divided their forces to round up the tribes, built forts and garrisons, and then advanced on Wukai.

sentences.zh: 請因兵力討水西奢香，不許。

translations.literal: He requested to take advantage of his military strength to campaign against She Xiang of Shuixi, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to use his army against She Xiang of Shuixi, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三十年三月，水西蠻居宗必登等作亂，會顧成討平之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirtieth year, the Shuixi tribesmen Ju Zong, Bideng, and others rose in rebellion; Gu Cheng happened to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirtieth year the Shuixi tribesmen Ju Zong, Bideng, and others rebelled; Gu Cheng was sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 其冬拜征虜左將軍，副西平侯沐春討麓川叛蠻刀幹孟。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Left General for the Campaign against the Barbarians and served as deputy to the Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun in the campaign against the Luchuan rebel tribesman Dao Ganmeng.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed Left General for the Campaign against the Barbarians and served under the Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun against the Luchuan rebel Dao Ganmeng.

sentences.zh: 明年，福與都督瞿能逾高良公山，搗南甸，擒其酋刀名孟。

translations.literal: The following year, Fu together with the regional commander Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year He Fu and the regional commander Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.

sentences.zh: 回軍擊景罕寨，不下。

translations.literal: On the return march they attacked Jinghan stockade but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march they attacked Jinghan stockade but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 春以銳軍至，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Chun arrived with crack troops and the bandits, startled, broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chun arrived with his elite troops and the rebels broke and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 幹孟懼，乞降。

translations.literal: Ganmeng was afraid and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Ganmeng, alarmed, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 已而春卒，賊復懷貳。

translations.literal: Before long Chun died, and the bandits again harbored double loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Mu Chun died, and the rebels wavered in their allegiance once more.

sentences.zh: 是時太祖已崩，惠帝初即位，拜福征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At this time the Taizu had already passed away and the Huandi had just ascended the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Campaign against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: By then the founding emperor had died and the Jianwen Emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Campaign against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 福遂破擒刀幹孟，降其眾七萬。

translations.literal: Fu thereupon broke through, captured Dao Ganmeng, and accepted the surrender of his masses numbering seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu then defeated and captured Dao Ganmeng and accepted the surrender of seventy thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 分兵徇下諸寨，麓川地悉定。

translations.literal: He divided his forces to subdue the various stockades below, and the territory of Luchuan was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to subdue the remaining stockades, and the whole of Luchuan was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，還京師，論功進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he returned to the capital; his merits were assessed and he was advanced to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwen he returned to the capital and was promoted to vice regional commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 練兵德州，進左都督。

translations.literal: He drilled troops at Dezhou and was advanced to Left Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He trained troops at Dezhou and was promoted to Left Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 與盛庸、平安會兵伐燕，戰淮北不利，奔還。

translations.literal: He joined forces with Sheng Yong and Ping An to campaign against Yan; fighting north of the Huai was unfavorable, and he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sheng Yong and Ping An in the campaign against Yan; defeated north of the Huai, he fled back.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，以福宿將知兵，推誠用之。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu ascended the throne, because Fu was a veteran general who understood warfare, he employed him with full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he trusted the veteran He Fu for his military experience and employed him with complete sincerity.

sentences.zh: 聘其甥女徐氏為趙王妃。

translations.literal: He betrothed Fu's niece, the Lady Xu, as consort to the Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He betrothed He Fu's niece Lady Xu to the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 尋，命佩征虜將軍印，充總兵官，鎮寧夏，節制山、陜、河南諸軍。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to wear the seal of General for the Campaign against the Barbarians, serve as supreme commander, garrison Ningxia, and exercise control over the armies of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the seal of General for the Campaign against the Barbarians, made supreme commander, and posted to Ningxia with authority over the armies of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 福至鎮，宣布德意，招徠遠人，塞外諸部降者相踵。

translations.literal: When Fu reached his post, he proclaimed the imperial virtue and intent, recruited distant peoples, and tribes beyond the frontier surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At his post He Fu proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intentions and drew in distant peoples; tribes beyond the frontier surrendered in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 邊陲無事，因請置驛、屯田、積谷，定賞罰，為經久計。

translations.literal: The frontier was without incident, and he thereupon requested the establishment of courier stations, military colonies, grain reserves, and fixed rewards and punishments as a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier at peace, he proposed establishing courier stations, military colonies, grain reserves, and fixed rules of reward and punishment as a long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 會有讒之者。

translations.literal: There happened to be those who slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers soon appeared.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，降敕褒慰。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen and issued an edict of praise and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed and sent an edict praising and reassuring him.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年八月，移鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Yongle he was transferred to garrison Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Yongle he was transferred to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 福馭軍嚴，下多不便者。

translations.literal: Fu commanded his army with severity, and many below found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu ran a tight army, and many of his subordinates resented his discipline.

sentences.zh: 帝間使使戒福，善自衛，毋為小人所中。

translations.literal: The Emperor from time to time sent envoys to warn Fu to guard himself well and not be struck down by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor occasionally sent word warning him to look to his own safety and not fall victim to petty intrigues.

sentences.zh: 六年，福請遣京師蕃將將迤北降人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Fu requested to send the frontier generals of the capital to command the surrendered peoples of the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year He Fu asked that frontier generals from the capital be sent to command the surrendered northern tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「爾久總蕃、漢兵，恐勢眾致讒耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, saying, "You have long commanded both barbarian and Han troops; I fear your great following invites slander.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "You have long commanded both tribal and Han troops; I fear your large following invites slander.

sentences.zh: 爾老將，朕推誠倚重，毋顧慮。

translations.literal: You are an old general; I rely on you with full sincerity — have no anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: You are a veteran general whom I trust completely — have no anxieties.

sentences.zh: 」尋請以布市馬，選其良者別為群，置官給印專領之。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he requested to use cloth to purchase horses, select the good ones and set them apart in separate herds, appoint officials and issue seals to have charge of them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: " He then proposed trading cloth for horses, selecting the best animals for separate herds, and appointing officials with seals to manage them.

sentences.zh: 於是馬大蕃息。

translations.literal: Thereupon horses greatly multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: The horse herds multiplied greatly.

sentences.zh: 永昌苑牧馬自此始。

translations.literal: The pasturing of horses at the Yongchang Park began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial horse pastures at Yongchang date from this period.

sentences.zh: 明年，本雅失裏糾阿魯臺將入寇，為瓦剌所敗，走臚朐河，欲收諸部潰卒窺河西。

translations.literal: The following year, Benyashiri rallied Aruqtai intending to invade, but was defeated by the Oirats, fled to the Lutong River, and wished to gather the scattered troops of the various tribes to spy on Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Benyashiri and Aruqtai planned an invasion but were defeated by the Oirats; Benyashiri fled to the Lutong River and tried to rally scattered tribesmen to probe the Hexi frontier.

sentences.zh: 詔福嚴兵為備。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu to keep his troops strict in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu was ordered to keep his army on full alert.

sentences.zh: 迤北王子、國公、司徒以下十余人帥所部駐亦集乃，乞內附。

translations.literal: More than ten persons including princes, state dukes, and situ of the northern frontier led their followers to encamp at Ejin and begged to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten northern princes, state dukes, and situ and their followers encamped at Ejin and asked to submit to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 福以聞，帝令庶子楊榮往，佐福經理，其眾悉降。

translations.literal: Fu reported this; the Emperor ordered the heir apparent's tutor Yang Rong to go and assist Fu in managing affairs, and all their masses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu reported this; the Emperor sent the heir apparent's tutor Yang Rong to assist him, and all the tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 福親至亦集乃鎮撫之，送其酋長於京師。

translations.literal: Fu personally went to Ejin to pacify and comfort them and sent their chieftains to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu went in person to Ejin to receive them and sent their chiefs to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉福功，命榮即軍中封福為寧遠侯，祿千石，且詔福軍中事先行後聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Fu's merit, ordered Rong to enfeoff Fu in the army as Marquis of Ningyuan with an income of one thousand piculs, and moreover decreed that in military affairs Fu might act first and report afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded his service, had Yang Rong enfeoff him in camp as Marquis of Ningyuan with a stipend of one thousand piculs, and authorized him to act first and report afterward in military matters.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，召福從出塞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor campaigned north and summoned Fu to follow beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Emperor marched north and summoned He Fu to accompany him beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以福有才略，寵任逾諸將。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor, because Fu had talent and stratagem, favored and entrusted him beyond the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had favored He Fu above other generals for his talent and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 福亦善引嫌，有事未嘗專決。

translations.literal: Fu also knew how to avoid suspicion; when there were matters he had never decided alone.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu was also careful to avoid arousing suspicion and never made important decisions on his own.

sentences.zh: 在鎮嘗請取西平侯家鞏昌蓄馬，以充孳牧。

translations.literal: While at his post he once requested to take the horses kept at Gongchang by the household of the Marquis of Xiping to supplement breeding herds.
translations.idiomatic: While in command he once asked to take horses kept at Gongchang by the Marquis of Xiping's household to replenish his breeding herds.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「皇考時貴近家多許養馬，以示共享富貴之意。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, saying, "In the time of the Imperial Father, the households of the honored and near were mostly permitted to keep horses, to show the intent of sharing wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Under my father's reign the great families were allowed to keep horses as a sign that wealth and honor were to be shared.

sentences.zh: 爾所奏固為國矣，然非待勛戚之道。

translations.literal: What you memorialized is indeed for the state, yet it is not the way to treat meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: Your proposal serves the state, but it is not how meritorious kinsmen should be treated.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 其余有請輒行，委寄甚重。

translations.literal: As for the rest, whenever he made a request it was carried out, and the trust placed in him was very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Other requests were routinely granted, and the trust placed in him was immense.

sentences.zh: 及從征，數違節度。

translations.literal: When he followed on campaign, he repeatedly violated regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, however, he repeatedly disobeyed orders.

sentences.zh: 群臣有言其罪者，福益怏怏有怨言。

translations.literal: When ministers spoke of his offenses, Fu grew all the more displeased and voiced complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers reported his misconduct, He Fu grew resentful and voiced complaints.

sentences.zh: 師還，都御史陳瑛復劾之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying again impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, the censor-in-chief Chen Ying impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 福懼，自縊死，爵除。

translations.literal: Fu was afraid and hanged himself; his enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu, in fear, hanged himself, and his title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 而趙王妃亦尋廢。

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Zhao was also before long deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao's consort was soon afterward deposed as well.

sentences.zh: 顧成，字景韶，其先湘潭人。

translations.literal: Gu Cheng, style name Jingshao, his ancestors were men of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng, style name Jingshao, was descended from a Xiangtan family.

sentences.zh: 祖父業操舟，往來江、淮間，遂家江都。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ye worked a boat, traveling back and forth between the Yangtze and Huai, and the family thereupon settled in Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ye was a boatman on the Yangtze and Huai routes, and the family eventually settled in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 成少魁岸，膂力絕人，善馬槊，文其身以自異。

translations.literal: Cheng in youth was tall and imposing, his physical strength surpassing other men; he was skilled with the cavalry lance and tattooed his body to set himself apart.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Gu Cheng was tall and powerfully built, skilled with the cavalry lance, and tattooed his body to mark himself as unusual.

sentences.zh: 太祖渡江，來歸，以勇選為帳前親兵，擎蓋出入。

translations.literal: When the Taizu crossed the Yangtze, he came to submit; for his courage he was selected as a personal guard before the tent, bearing the canopy in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor crossed the Yangtze, Gu Cheng joined him and, for his courage, was chosen as a personal guard who bore the imperial canopy on campaign.

sentences.zh: 嘗從上出，舟膠於沙，成負舟而行。

translations.literal: Once when he followed the sovereign on an outing, the boat stuck in sand; Cheng carried the boat on his back and walked.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was afloat, the boat ran aground in sand and Gu Cheng shouldered it and waded ashore with it.

sentences.zh: 從攻鎮江，與勇士十人轉鬥入城，被執，十人皆死。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Zhenjiang; with ten brave men he fought in successive engagements into the city, was captured, and the ten all died.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Zhenjiang he fought his way into the city with ten picked men, was captured, and all ten of his companions were killed.

sentences.zh: 成躍起斷縛，仆持刀者，脫歸。

translations.literal: Cheng leaped up, broke his bonds, threw down the man holding the blade, and escaped back.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng broke his bonds, knocked down the man with the blade, and fought his way back to his own lines.

sentences.zh: 導眾攻城，克之，授百戶。

translations.literal: He guided the masses in attacking the city and took it; he was appointed centurion.
translations.idiomatic: He led the assault that took the city and was appointed a centurion.

sentences.zh: 大小數十戰，皆有功，進堅城衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In several dozen battles large and small he had merit in each; he was advanced to assistant commander of the Jiancheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in dozens of engagements and was promoted to assistant commander of the Jiancheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 從伐蜀，攻羅江，擒元帥以下二十余人，進降漢州。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the marshal and more than twenty others below him, and advanced to accept the surrender of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shu campaign he attacked Luojiang, captured the Yuan marshal and more than twenty officers, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，改成都後衛。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was transferred to the Chengdu Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was transferred to the Chengdu Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，擒重慶妖賊王元保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu he captured the Chongqing sorcerer-rebel Wang Yuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu he captured the Chongqing rebel sorcerer Wang Yuanbao.

sentences.zh: 八年調守貴州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to garrison Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時群蠻叛服不常，成連歲出兵，悉平之。

translations.literal: At that time the various tribes rebelled and submitted irregularly; Cheng year after year led troops out and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of the region rebelled and submitted by turns; Gu Cheng campaigned year after year until all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 已，從潁川侯傅友德征雲南，為前鋒，首克普定，留成列柵以守。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde in the campaign against Yunnan as vanguard, was first to take Puding, and Cheng was left to array stockades in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde against Yunnan as vanguard, was first to take Puding, and was left behind to build stockades and hold the position.

sentences.zh: 蠻數萬來攻，成出柵，手殺數十百人，賊退走。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of tribesmen came to attack; Cheng went out of the stockade and with his own hand killed several tens and hundreds of men; the bandits retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of tribesmen attacked, Gu Cheng sallied from the stockade and killed scores of them with his own hand; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 余賊猶在南城，成斬所俘而縱其一，曰：「吾夜二鼓來殺汝。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits were still at the south wall; Cheng beheaded those he had captured and released one, saying, "At the second watch tonight I shall come to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors still held the south wall; Gu Cheng executed his prisoners but spared one, telling him, "I will come at the second watch tonight to kill you.

sentences.zh: 」夜二鼓，吹角鳴炮，賊聞悉走，獲器甲無算。

translations.literal: " At the second watch of night he blew horns and fired cannon; when the bandits heard this they all fled, and weapons and armor captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: " At the second watch he sounded horns and fired cannon; the enemy fled in panic, leaving arms and armor beyond count.

sentences.zh: 進指揮使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻隸普定者悉平。

translations.literal: All the tribes subordinate to Puding were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All the tribes under Puding's jurisdiction were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十七年，平阿黑、螺螄等十余寨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he pacified more than ten stockades including Ahei and Luosi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he pacified more than ten stockades, including those of Ahei and Luosi.

sentences.zh: 明年奏罷普定府，析其地為三州、六長官司。

translations.literal: The following year he memorialized to abolish Puding Prefecture and divide its territory into three subprefectures and six native-official districts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized to abolish Puding Prefecture and reorganize its territory into three subprefectures and six native-official districts.

sentences.zh: 進貴州都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice regional commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice regional commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 有告其受賕及僭用玉器等物者，以久勞不問。

translations.literal: There were those who reported that he had accepted bribes and presumptuously used jade vessels and other objects; because of his long service he was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He was accused of taking bribes and improperly using jade vessels and the like, but because of his long service the charges were not pursued.

sentences.zh: 二十九年遷右軍都督僉事，佩征南將軍印。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to assistant regional commander of the Right Army and wore the seal of General for the Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to assistant regional commander of the Right Army and given the seal of General for the Southern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 會何福討水西蠻，斬其酋居宗必登。

translations.literal: He happened to join He Fu in campaigning against the Shuixi tribes and beheaded the chieftain Ju Zong Bideng.
translations.idiomatic: He joined He Fu in the campaign against the Shuixi tribes and helped behead the chieftain Ju Zong Bideng.

sentences.zh: 明年，西堡、滄浪諸寨蠻亂，成遣指揮陸秉與其子統分道討平之。

translations.literal: The following year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; Cheng dispatched the commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; Gu Cheng sent the commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 成在貴州凡十余年，討平諸苗洞寨以百數，皆誅其渠魁，撫綏余眾。

translations.literal: Cheng was in Guizhou for more than ten years in all, campaigning to pacify several hundred Miao cave-stockades; in each case he executed the ringleaders and comforted and settled the remaining masses.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng spent more than ten years in Guizhou, pacifying several hundred Miao stockades; in each case he executed the ringleaders and won over the rest.

sentences.zh: 恩信大布，蠻人帖服。

translations.literal: His grace and trust were broadly displayed, and the tribesmen submitted in docility.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence and reliability won wide recognition, and the tribes submitted peacefully.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，召還京。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 成性忠謹，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: Cheng by nature was loyal and prudent and dipped into books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng was loyal and prudent by nature and well read in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 始居北平，多效謀畫，然終不肯將兵，賜兵器亦不受。

translations.literal: When he first resided at Beiping he often offered plans and stratagems, yet in the end he would not command troops, and weapons bestowed on him he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When he first lived at Beiping he often offered strategic advice, but he always refused to take command of troops and would not even accept weapons bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 再鎮貴州，屢平播州、都勻諸叛蠻，威鎮南中，土人立生祠祀焉。

translations.literal: When he again garrisoned Guizhou, he repeatedly pacified the rebellious tribes of Bozhou, Duyun, and others; his authority dominated the southern interior, and the local people erected living shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Posted again to Guizhou, he repeatedly suppressed rebellions in Bozhou, Duyun, and elsewhere; his authority dominated the south, and the local people built shrines in his honor while he was still alive.

sentences.zh: 其被召至京也，命輔太子監國。

translations.literal: When he was summoned to the capital, he was ordered to assist the heir apparent in overseeing the state.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to the capital, he was ordered to assist the crown prince in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 成頓首言：「太子仁明，廷臣皆賢，輔導之事非愚臣所及，請歸備蠻。

translations.literal: Cheng bowed his head to the ground and said, "The heir apparent is benevolent and enlightened, and the court ministers are all worthy; matters of guidance and instruction are beyond this foolish servant — I beg to return and guard against the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng kowtowed and said, "The crown prince is benevolent and wise, and the court ministers are all capable; guidance is beyond this humble servant's ability — I beg leave to return to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」時群小謀奪嫡，太子不自安。

translations.literal: " At that time petty men plotted to seize the succession, and the heir apparent was not at ease in himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Petty schemers were then plotting to displace the heir, and the crown prince lived in anxiety.

sentences.zh: 成入辭文華殿，因曰：「殿下但當竭誠孝敬，孳孳恤民。

translations.literal: When Cheng entered to take leave at the Wenhua Hall, he thereupon said, "Your Highness need only exhaust sincerity in filial respect and diligently care for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave at the Wenhua Hall, he told the prince, "Your Highness need only devote yourself to filial duty and care tirelessly for the people.

sentences.zh: 萬事在天，小人不足措意。

translations.literal: All affairs rest with Heaven; petty men are not worth setting one's mind on.
translations.idiomatic: All else rests with Heaven; petty men are not worth your concern.

sentences.zh: 」十二年五月卒，年八十有五。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the fifth month of the twelfth year, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈夏國公，謚武毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xia with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xia with the posthumous title Resolute in War.

sentences.zh: 八子。

translations.literal: He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長統，普定衛指揮，以成降燕被誅。

translations.literal: The eldest, Tong, was commander of the Puding Guard; because Cheng surrendered to Yan he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Tong, was commander of the Puding Guard; he was executed because Gu Cheng had surrendered to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 從弟溥嗣，掌五軍右掖。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Pu succeeded him and directed the Right Rear Army of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Pu succeeded to the family line and directed the Right Rear Army of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，拜平蠻將軍，鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Tribes and garrisoned Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Tribes and posted to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 始至，捕斬苗中首惡。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he captured and beheaded the chief evildoers among the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he captured and executed the worst offenders among the Miao.

sentences.zh: 五年十月，貴州都勻苗乜富架作亂，自稱都順王，梗滇、蜀道。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year the Duyun Miao of Guizhou, Yefujia, rose in rebellion, styled himself King of Dushun, and blocked the routes of Yunnan and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year the Duyun Miao chieftain Yefujia rebelled in Guizhou, proclaimed himself King of Dushun, and cut the roads between Yunnan and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔溥充總兵官，帥兵八萬討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pu to serve as supreme commander and lead eighty thousand troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was ordered to serve as supreme commander and lead eighty thousand troops against him.

sentences.zh: 分五路刻期並進，誅富架父子，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: He divided into five routes with a fixed date for simultaneous advance, executed Yefujia father and son, and beheaded them by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his force into five columns that advanced on a fixed schedule, killed Yefujia and his son, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，增祿二百石。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and his stipend was increased by two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and his stipend was increased by two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 召入提督團營，掌前軍都督府事。

translations.literal: He was summoned in to supervise the training corps and directed the affairs of the Front Army regional command.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to supervise the training corps and to direct the Front Army regional command.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 謚襄恪。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiangke.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Respectful and Diligent.

sentences.zh: 溥清慎守法，卒之日，囊無余資，英國公張懋出布帛以斂。

translations.literal: Pu was pure, cautious, and observant of law; on the day of his death his purse held no surplus funds, and the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao provided cloth and silk for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was upright, cautious, and law-abiding; when he died his purse was empty, and the Duke of Ying Zhang Mao provided cloth and silk for his burial.

sentences.zh: 子仕隆嗣，管神機營左哨，得士心。

translations.literal: His son Shilong succeeded him, directed the Left Company of the Divine Engine Corps, and won the hearts of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilong succeeded him, commanded the Left Company of the firearms corps, and won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 正德初，出為漕運總兵，數請恤軍卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he went out as supreme commander of grain transport and repeatedly requested relief for soldiers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was appointed supreme commander of the grain transport and repeatedly petitioned for better treatment of the transport troops.

sentences.zh: 鎮淮安十余年，以清白聞。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Huaian for more than ten years and was known for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted at Huaian for more than ten years and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，江彬橫甚，折辱諸大吏，惟仕隆不為屈。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong made his southern tour, Jiang Bin was extremely overbearing and humiliated the great officials — only Shilong would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor toured the south, Jiang Bin bullied the high officials with impunity — only Shilong refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，移鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was transferred to garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，論奉迎防守功。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was summoned back and his merit was assessed for escorting and defending.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and rewarded for his service in escorting and defending the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 加太子太傅，掌中軍都督府事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and directed the affairs of the Central Army regional command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge of the Central Army regional command.

sentences.zh: 錦衣千戶王邦奇者，怨大學士楊廷和、兵部尚書彭澤，上疏言：「哈密失策，事由兩人。

translations.literal: Wang Bangqi, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, bore resentment against the Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and the Minister of War Peng Ze; he submitted a memorial saying, "The failure of policy at Hami arose from these two men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangqi, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, bore a grudge against Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and Minister of War Peng Ze and memorialized the throne: "The Hami debacle was their doing.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，逮系廷和諸子婿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was angry and arrested and imprisoned Tinghe's sons and sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was enraged and had Yang Tinghe's sons and sons-in-law arrested.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊言疏救，忤旨。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Yang Yan submitted a memorial in rescue, contrary to the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Yang Yan memorialized in their defense and offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 事下五府九卿科道議，仕隆言：「廷和功在社稷。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for deliberation by the Five Offices, Nine Ministers, and the censorial and supervising corps; Shilong said, "Tinghe's merit lies in the altars of state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Five Offices, Nine Ministers, and the censorial corps for deliberation; Shilong declared, "Yang Tinghe's service to the state has been immense.

sentences.zh: 邦奇小人，假邊事惑聖聽，傷國體。

translations.literal: Bangqi is a petty man who, under pretense of frontier affairs, deludes the sage ear and injures the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangqi is a petty man who uses frontier affairs to mislead the throne and damage the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 」有詔切責，移病解營務。

translations.literal: " An edict sharply rebuked him, and he pleaded illness to resign his camp duties.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict sharply rebuked him, and he resigned his command on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚榮靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Honored and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子寰嗣，守備南京。

translations.literal: His son Huan succeeded him and served as garrison commander of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan succeeded him and served as garrison commander of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 奉詔讞獄，多所平反。

translations.literal: By imperial order he reviewed prison cases and reversed many wrongful judgments.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he reviewed prison cases and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 十七年為漕運總兵官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he became supreme commander of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed supreme commander of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 明年，獻皇后梓宮赴承天，漕舟以避梓宮後期者三千。

translations.literal: The following year, when the empress's coffin went to Chengtian, three thousand grain-transport boats were delayed because they gave way to the coffin procession.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the empress's coffin was conveyed to Chengtian, three thousand grain barges fell behind schedule because they had to yield to the funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 而江南北多災傷，寰請被災地停漕一年，令改折色，軍民交便。

translations.literal: Yet north and south of the Yangtze there were many disasters and injuries; Huan requested that in disaster-stricken areas grain transport be halted for one year and conversion to monetary payment ordered, to the mutual convenience of army and people.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had struck both north and south of the Yangtze; Huan petitioned to suspend the grain transport for one year in the affected regions and substitute monetary payments, to the relief of soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 又條上漕政七事，並施行。

translations.literal: He also itemized seven matters on grain-transport administration and submitted them; all were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted seven proposals for reforming the transport system, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 諸為漕蠹者病之，遂布蜚語，為給事中王交所劾。

translations.literal: Those who were parasites on the grain transport resented this and thereupon spread slanderous rumors; he was impeached by the supervising secretary Wang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Those who profited from abuses in the transport system resented him and spread slander; the supervising secretary Wang Jiao impeached him.

sentences.zh: 已，按驗不實，再鎮淮安。

translations.literal: Before long, investigation verified that the charges were not true, and he was again garrisoned at Huaian.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved the charges false, and he was posted again to Huaian.

sentences.zh: 會安南事起，移鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: When the Annam affair arose, he was transferred to garrison the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out in Annam, he was transferred to the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 莫宏瀷者，安南都統使莫福海子也。

translations.literal: Mo Hongli was the son of Mo Fuhai, regional commander of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Hongli was the son of Mo Fuhai, the Annamese regional commander.

sentences.zh: 福海死，宏瀷幼。

translations.literal: When Fuhai died, Hongli was young.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuhai died, Hongli was still a child.

sentences.zh: 其權臣阮敬與族人莫正中構兵，國內亂，正中逃入欽州。

translations.literal: His powerful minister Ruan Jing and his clansman Mo Zhengzhong raised troops against each other; the state fell into disorder, and Zhengzhong fled into Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful minister Ruan Jing and a kinsman, Mo Zhengzhong, fought each other; the country fell into civil war, and Zhengzhong fled to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有議乘釁取安南者，寰與提督侍郎周延決策，請於朝，令宏瀷襲都統使，安南遂定。

translations.literal: At that time there were those who argued to seize the opportunity and take Annam; Huan together with the supervising grand coordinator Zhou Yan decided on policy, requested the court, and ordered Hongli to inherit the post of regional commander; Annam was thereupon stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Some at court urged seizing the opportunity to conquer Annam; Huan and the grand coordinator Zhou Yan decided instead to petition the throne to confirm Hongli as regional commander, and Annam was stabilized.

sentences.zh: 三十年事也。

translations.literal: This was a matter of the thirtieth year.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the thirtieth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 尋以兵討平桂林、平樂叛瑤。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter with troops he campaigned and pacified the rebellious Yao of Guilin and Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led troops to suppress rebellious Yao tribes in Guilin and Pingle.

sentences.zh: 復命鎮淮，有禦倭功。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to garrison Huai and had merit in repelling the Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted again to the Huai region and distinguished himself against the wokou pirates.

sentences.zh: 入總京營，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He entered to take overall charge of the capital garrison and was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to command the capital garrison and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 復出督漕。

translations.literal: He again went out to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out again to supervise the grain transport.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: He was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 請老。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，特起授京營總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he was specially raised and appointed governor of the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing he was specially recalled and appointed governor of the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋乞休。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire again.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，起掌左府。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong succeeded to the throne, he was raised to direct the Left regional command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was recalled to direct the Left Army regional command.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 加少保。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚榮僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Honored and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 自溥至寰三世，皆寬和廉靖，內行飭謹，曉文藝。

translations.literal: From Pu to Huan across three generations, all were magnanimous, gentle, pure, and tranquil; their private conduct was disciplined and careful, and they understood literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: From Pu through Huan across three generations, the family was known for magnanimity, integrity, disciplined private conduct, and literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 仕隆、寰兩世督漕，皆勤於職。

translations.literal: Shilong and Huan across two generations supervised grain transport and in each case were diligent in duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and Huan each served as transport commander and were diligent in their duties.

sentences.zh: 三傳至孫肇跡，京師陷，死於賊。

translations.literal: The line passed three generations to the grandson Zhaoji; when the capital fell he died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later the great-grandson Zhaoji died fighting the rebels when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：東昌、小河之戰，盛庸、平安屢挫燕師，斬其驍將，厥功甚壯。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In the battles of Dongchang and the Xiao River, Sheng Yong and Ping An repeatedly checked the Yan army and beheaded its valiant generals; their achievements were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: At Dongchang and the Xiao River, Sheng Yong and Ping An repeatedly turned back the Yan army and killed its finest commanders — a magnificent achievement.

sentences.zh: 及至兵敗被執，不克引義自裁，隱忍偷生，視鐵鉉、暴昭輩，能無愧乎？

translations.literal: Yet when they came to military defeat and capture, they could not take righteousness and cut themselves off; they endured in concealment and stole life — compared with Tie Xuan, Bao Zhao, and their kind, can they be without shame?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when defeat brought capture, they could not bring themselves to die for principle; they clung to life in disgrace. Compared with Tie Xuan, Bao Zhao, and men like them, how can they hold their heads high?

sentences.zh: 何福、顧成皆太祖時宿將，著功邊僥。

translations.literal: He Fu and Gu Cheng were both veteran generals of the Taizu's time who achieved merit on the frontier marches.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu and Gu Cheng were both veteran generals of the founding reign who won distinction on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 而一遇燕兵，或引卻南奔，或身遭俘馘。

translations.literal: Yet once they met the Yan army, one drew back and fled south, the other personally suffered capture and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they met the Yan army, one retreated south in defeat and the other was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 成祖棄瑕錄舊，均列茅土，亦雲幸矣。

translations.literal: The Chengzu set aside flaws and recorded old service; all alike were ranked among the fief-holders — this also may be called fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor overlooked their faults for past service and enfeoffed them alike — they were fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 福固不以功名終，而成之延及苗裔，榮不勝辱，亦奚足取哉。

translations.literal: Fu indeed did not end in fame and achievement, yet Cheng's line extended to descendants — when honor cannot overcome disgrace, what is there worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: He Fu did not end his career in glory, yet Gu Cheng's line endured for generations; when honor cannot outweigh disgrace, what is there to admire?
